newsitem.title: USA: Smaller DBS TV satellite to come from German firm.
newsitem.headline: Smaller DBS TV satellite to come from German firm.

text.p: A German technology company will on Tuesday announce in New York a competitor to the vastly popular direct-broadcast-satellite (DBS) dishes manufactured by Sony Corp and Thomson SA.

Galaxis Holding GmBh of Lubeck said its Future 1 Planar Satellite Antenna is smaller than a notebook and can receive both DBS transmissions from space satellites and wireless cable, or microwave television, signals.
The flat antenna is 15-1/2 inches by 8-1/2 by 1-1/2 and can receive more than 100 digital and analog television stations, as well as radio transmissions, Galaxis said in a news release.

A spokesman for Galaxis said the antenna's reception was also impervious to weather interference, a mark against the DBS dishes launched in 1994 in the United States. More than three million DBS units are in use in the United States.
Galaxis, manufacturer and developer of communications equipment, will likely license its Future 1 technology rather than manufacture the devices itself, the spokesman said.
Pricing and a rollout schedule have not been decided, the spokesman said.

"We are currently working on distribution agreements and manufacturing partnerships to ensure that we can deliver the highest quality technology at the most economic price levels ...," Galaxis senior vice president Jim Clingham said.
The spokesman said at least one U.S. telephone company working on wireless-cable delivery of filmed entertainment was a potential buyer of Galaxis devices.

Sony and Thomson now supply DBS receivers and dishes and will be joined by year's end by other manufacturers such as Toshiba Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial trying to exploit a recent round of price cuts on DBS equipment.
